Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.desktop2d

Class DesktopSwing

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.desktop2d.Desktop2D
org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.desktop2d.DesktopSwing
public class DesktopSwing extends Desktop2D
The conventional Swing desktop: the same MDI shell as Desktop2D - one maximised window whose JDesktopPane hosts each application in a JInternalFrame - but wearing the Metal look and feel.

Why the windows are JInternalFrames, not top-level JFrames. A JFrame is a native, top-level window owned by the host window manager: it cannot be a child of a JDesktopPane, and minimising it iconifies it into the host taskbar, outside the desktop. The only Swing window that lives inside a JDesktopPane - and so stays within the desktop, cascades with its siblings, and minimises into an icon on the desktop rather than escaping it - is JInternalFrame. That is stock Swing (the classic MDI pattern), not custom chrome, so using it is the opposite of reinventing the wheel: it is the component Swing provides for exactly this "windows integrated into a desktop pane" job.

Everything is inherited from Desktop2D unchanged - the wallpaper JDesktopPane, the internal-frame hosting and de-duplication (Desktop2DWindow), the start menu, the Documents/Downloads folder menus, the taskbar with its per-window buttons, external-command and conventional-Swing-app launches, and exit handling. This subclass adds only the Metal look and feel and its own window title, so the two flavours cannot drift apart. --2d keeps the host system look and feel.
